# vk 0.13.5 — Inlined publication and single admission

Development release, 2026-11-26. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.13.5+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.13.5`**, MIT licensed.
The Vulkan header snapshot remains 1.4.365; it is not a minimum driver version.
Public function names, signatures and error payloads are unchanged.

## Allocator changes

Publication and its registry insertion were separate calls that received a
caller-built region record by reference and assembled the 248-byte live
record on the stack before copying it into the registry slot with
overlapping 16-byte moves. Those loads read bytes written by narrower stores
and failed store-to-load forwarding. Both are now inlined into their callers;
VTune `LD_BLOCKS.STORE_FORWARD` counts in vk code fell from 16.8 to 12.8 per
pooled operation on the recorded device.

`allocate_native` repeated the export admission (`allocation_exports`) that
every caller — separate storage, pooled growth and custom-pool minimum blocks —
had just performed for the same memory type and chain; the repeat is removed.
Managed creation reserves publication before native effects, and
`allocate_storage` no longer reserves a second time. The public raw
`allocate` now reserves before entering the shared storage path. A
partitioned allocator therefore consumes one shared serial per publication
instead of two. Error order for ordinary inputs is unchanged.

## Measured results

The complete [Surface Laptop 5 report](../benchmarks/surface-laptop-5-2026-11-26.md)
retains the committed-tree matrix, both backend build identities, the
November 22 comparison, kept and rejected experiments and validation runs.

On the latest matrix (20 fresh-process samples per cell, unlocked clocks,
shared workstation with a crash-looping desktop indexer): **23 of 44 combined
workloads complete below 1.0× VMA**, the same count as v0.13.4. 23 of the 30
native-resource cells improved and their geometric-mean ratio moved from
1.022 to 1.007. Cells more than 5% slower than VMA fall from 9 to 3:
separate-buffer churn moves from 1.100 to 1.033, pooled-buffer TLSF churn
from 1.091 to 1.024 and pooled-buffer reverse/FIFO to 0.923–0.931. The worst
measured gap is pooled-buffer linear shuffle at 1.091 (interval
0.980–1.172), which measured 1.022 on November 22. The below-0.9× target
across the suite is not met.

## Correctness

All 44 benchmark cells pass under separate core and synchronization
validation on the committed tree. The 3,463-test workspace suite passes on
the recorded device. Strict workspace Clippy, formatting and
`git diff --check` pass. These results qualify the named workloads on this
machine, not Vulkan conformance, other devices/drivers or the full feature
set.
